role: A successor to retention-tiers.v24 designing against two pieces of product intent recorded on 2026-08-05. First: retention is bounded by time, size and count, the bounds are per-project and configurable, tombstones survive, and a PURGED state must say why. Second, and overturning the premise v24's Part A was built on: retention is DURABLE BY DEFAULT and unbounded unless configured, so a project with no configured policy retains durably and a durable-authoritative request with no policy proceeds and writes rather than refusing. This artifact adds TRIGGERS to the existing PURGED transition, closes the cause partition so absence is explainable, and repairs the three surfaces of Part A that the posture decision overturns. It is not a deletion model: purge here is already capability degradation on a record that stays addressable.

statedShape: Retention is bounded by time AND size, both configurable, per project.
Count is also a dimension, and in the shipping product it is the primary one; it is recovered from that product rather than stated by the owner.
Tombstones survive: when a bound fires the record transitions to PURGED, bytes may be reclaimed, and the tombstone remains so absence is always explainable.
A PURGED state must carry why: aged out, size pressure, count pressure, or user request.

A project with no configured policy retains durably.
A durable-authoritative request with no policy PROCEEDS AND WRITES rather than refusing.
clauses.howTheChoiceWasPut: Two options with their costs side by side. The entire difference: someone runs the tool having configured nothing and the run needs durable evidence -- refuse and write nothing, or run and write to their disk. No middle option existed, because v24's own whyNotSimplyProceedEphemeral records that silently producing ephemeral evidence for a durable-authoritative request is a durability failure reporting authoritative success, which freeze law 14 forbids.
clauses.consequenceTheOwnerWasToldAndAccepted: The tool writes analysis evidence into a user's project before that user has been asked. This is the intended behaviour, not a side effect.

overriddenArchitecturalRecommendation.whyTheOverrideIsLegitimate: The recommendation's own declared status was AWAITING-PRODUCT-DISPOSITION. Architecture recommends and the product authority decides; the authority is not bound by the preference and a recommendation that could not be overridden would not be a recommendation. This is the mechanism working.

whatTheOverrideCosts.statement: The recommendation existed for a reason and the reason does not evaporate because it was overruled. v22's position was that no managed durable user-derived write should happen without an explicit policy. Under the new default exactly that happens, on first run, before any question is asked.
namedExposures: A user who runs the tool once, having configured nothing, has analysis evidence written durably into their project without having been asked first.
Combined with bounds defaulting to unbounded, the default configuration is MAXIMAL retention: keep everything, forever, until someone configures otherwise.
Combined with the append-only ledger, which no bound may touch, a project that is never configured grows monotonically and without limit.
whatMitigatesThem: The ask still happens at the first local-interactive durable-authoritative run, so the un-asked window is bounded by the first interactive use rather than lasting forever.
The default is never persisted, so a user who is later asked answers a genuinely open question rather than confirming something already written on their behalf.
Purge remains available and remains degradation rather than deletion, so retention is reversible in the capability sense even though the tombstone is not.
whatTheOverrideCosts.whatDoesNotMitigateThem: Nothing here reduces what is written before the first ask. The exposure is real, it was stated to the authority in those terms, and the authority accepted it. This artifact records it rather than softening it.

overriddenArchitecturalRecommendation.whatArchitectureMayNotDoAboutIt: It may not re-litigate the decision by designing a mechanism that quietly restores the recommendation -- for instance by defaulting bounds aggressively so that durable-by-default becomes durable-briefly. Bounds default to unbounded precisely so that this artifact does not smuggle back the position the authority rejected.

theKeyProperty.statement: EPHEMERAL_ONLY is reachable only with provenance CONSENTED. There is no input for which the resolution returns (EPHEMERAL_ONLY, DEFAULTED).
theKeyProperty.whyItMatters: It is what makes the surviving refusal path defensible. After this change the only request that is still refused for retention reasons is a durable-authoritative request under EPHEMERAL_ONLY, and this property says that case always means a person was asked and declined. The tool never refuses on the strength of a posture nobody chose.

whyAResolutionRuleAndNotASchemaField: A default field on ProjectRetentionPolicyV1 would replicate the default into every project's record, so changing it would mean migrating N records rather than editing one function.

It would also make the record's field set depend on the default's existence, which changes the record shape and therefore its identity recipe -- the freeze law 6 problem the bounds record already avoids.
Worst, it would make the default indistinguishable from a choice once written. A field holding DURABLE_RETAINED cannot say whether a person typed it.
postureResolution.whyNotAStatedFallback: A fallback stated only in prose is exactly the thing that drifts. It cannot be computed, cannot be tested, and cannot be pointed at by a second reader. The corpus has a standing answer to this shape and it is to make the value derived.

theDefaultIsNeverPersisted.rule: no code path writes a ProjectRetentionPolicyV1 whose posture came from the default
theDefaultIsNeverPersisted.whyThisMattersMost: It keeps ABSENT a real storage state. A user who has never been asked has no policy on disk, so when they are eventually asked they answer an open question rather than confirming a record already written in their name. Persisting the default would manufacture consent provenance that no human supplied, which is the CONSENTED/DEFAULTED distinction collapsing at exactly the point it is load bearing.
theDefaultIsNeverPersisted.secondConsequence: Because the default is never persisted, reversing this product decision later requires changing one function and migrating nothing. Had the default been written into each project's record, a reversal would have to distinguish records that hold DURABLE_RETAINED because someone chose it from records that hold it because the tool wrote it -- a distinction that would no longer exist.

hasNoDefaultField.predecessorJustificationVerbatim: A default field is a place a durable-retention default can be written without a product decision. CD-RT-5 owns that choice and remains BLOCKED_ON_PHASE_1A, so the schema does not provide the field.
hasNoDefaultField.whyThatJustificationIsDead: It rested on the choice being unmade. The authority has now made it. The reason the field is still absent is completely different and must not be allowed to inherit the old sentence.
hasNoDefaultField.replacementJustification: The record still has no default field, because a default belongs in a total resolution function where it is stated once and derived, not replicated into every project's record where it could not be told apart from a choice.
hasNoDefaultField.whatIsExplicitlyWithdrawn: the stronger reading that no default exists anywhere in the system. A default now exists. It lives in effective_posture and is named DEFAULTED.

absenceIsADistinctState.withdrawnAsAPostureClaim: Absence no longer means there is no posture. It resolves to DURABLE_RETAINED, the same posture a consenting user would produce.
absenceIsADistinctState.survivesAsAProvenanceClaim: ABSENT and a recorded DURABLE_RETAINED remain genuinely different states. They agree on posture and differ on provenance: DEFAULTED against CONSENTED. The distinction moved from the posture axis to the provenance axis; it did not disappear.
absenceIsADistinctState.whyItMustSurviveSomewhere: Consent provenance is the whole subject of Part A. If ABSENT and CONSENTED DURABLE_RETAINED became the same state, the system would lose the ability to say whether anyone was ever asked, and the first-run ask would become unobservable in its own outputs.

postureEnum.whyNoThirdMember: ABSENT was never a posture enum member and does not become one. It is the absence of a record, and it is now an INPUT to the resolution rather than an output of it. Adding it to the enum would make every consumer branch on a state the resolution exists to remove.

Proceeding durably would override a recorded human answer. Proceeding ephemerally while reporting authoritative success is law 14's first clause exactly. Refusing is the only remaining honest option, so the refusal is not a leftover -- it is the case the refusal was always for.
theRefusalPathSurvivesAndMoves.netEffect: The refusal moves from the un-consulted case to the consulted-and-declined case. It becomes rarer and better justified. It does not disappear, and an implementation that deleted it would violate law 14 in the direction the default was never meant to license.

noAskCasesReDerived.whyTheRefusalWasThereBefore: v24's reason was that proceeding would mean choosing a retention default. That was correct while no default existed. A default now exists and was chosen by the authority, so proceeding no longer chooses anything.
noAskCasesReDerived.whatIsNowExposedThatWasNotBefore: CI runs on machines nobody is sitting at, and CI is the profile that can never be asked. So CI is precisely where durable evidence is now written with provenance DEFAULTED and no prospect of the provenance ever becoming CONSENTED by that path. noAskCasesReDerived.name: the run that triggers the prompt
noAskCasesReDerived.predecessorChoiceVerbatim: REFUSE-TO-START-UNTIL-ANSWERED, with the ask relocated to request-validation
whatSurvives: The relocation of the ask to request-validation survives completely.

Its justification never rested on the default. It rested on the admission boundary: asking at request-validation means there is no ExecutionId, no AttemptRecord, no SnapshotId, no PlanId, no ExecutionPlan and no Run at ask time, so there is nothing to buffer and nothing to discard.

Both rejected alternatives stay rejected for their original reasons: buffering leaves user-derived evidence in host memory reaching swap and the page cache, which DeletionProtocol cannot erase; discard-and-re-run doubles the work and leaves a partial execution unrecorded.
The ask remains a host effect at request-validation, so freeze law 5 is untouched and the core still never sees the policy or the prompt.
noAskCasesReDerived.whatChanges: REFUSE-TO-START-UNTIL-ANSWERED becomes ASK-BUT-DO-NOT-BLOCK. The question is still asked at the same point; not answering it no longer stops the run.
noAskCasesReDerived.whyTheRelocationStillMattersEvenWithoutT: This is the part most at risk of being discarded as collateral. The relocation was never a mechanism for refusing; it was a mechanism for ensuring the question is asked at a point where the answer can still govern everything that follows. With a default in place the answer governs whether provenance becomes CONSENTED and whether a policy is persisted at all, both of which still need to be settled before an ExecutionId exists. Asking later would mean a run that had already written durably under DEFAULTED asking a question whose answer could no longer change what it did.

whatSurvives: Closing the dialog is still not an answer.
No dismissal path writes a policy. This survives and becomes MORE important, not less.
A non-TTY stdout or a non-terminal stdin still forces profile ci rather than being a dismissal, and a controlling terminal still never promotes an invocation to local-interactive.
noAskCasesReDerived.whatChanges: a dismissal no longer terminates the request; the run proceeds durably under DEFAULTED

thePolarityReversalThatMattersMost.predecessorReasonVerbatim: A dismissal that silenced the next ask would become EPHEMERAL_ONLY by attrition.
thePolarityReversalThatMattersMost.successorReason: A dismissal that silenced the next ask would become DURABLE_RETAINED by attrition: the user is never asked again, and their project is retained durably and unboundedly forever without anyone ever having consented.
thePolarityReversalThatMattersMost.whyThisStrengthensTheRuleRatherThanWeake: Under the old default, attrition drifted toward retaining less than the user might have wanted -- an annoyance. Under the new default, attrition drifts toward retaining data the user was never asked about -- a consent failure. The same rule, dismissalSuppressesTheNextAsk false, now guards a materially more serious failure, so an implementer tempted to relax it for user-experience reasons should read this paragraph first.

noAskCasesReDerived.whyNoDismissalPathWritingAPolicyMattersM: If a dismissal wrote DURABLE_RETAINED, it would manufacture CONSENTED provenance from a person declining to answer. The posture would be the same either way, which is exactly what makes the error easy to commit and hard to see: only the provenance field would be wrong, and only the provenance field records whether anyone was asked.

partC_retentionBounds.subject: the triggers that fire the already-specified PURGED transition, the closed cause partition that makes a PURGED state say why, and the subordinate closed record that carries the configured bounds

whyThisIsSmallerThanItLooks.claim: Purge in this corpus is not deletion. It is capability degradation on a record that stays addressable. The transition, the terminal state, the tombstone, the read-time derivation and the typed refusal all already exist and were independently verified. What did not exist is what makes the transition FIRE, and what makes it SAY WHY.
evidenceInThePredecessor: AF-03-VERIFY-PURGED is a state PURGED override that keeps its recordCasRef, so the record is still named after the purge.
The availability state lattice already carries PURGED as its single terminal state, with reversibility false.
UnitAvailabilityLedgerV1 is already append-only, and its terminal rule already makes a PURGED entry permanent.
AvailabilityTransitionV1 already carries a cause field in ordered position 7.
The typed refusal kind RETENTION_EVIDENCE_PURGED already exists and already has refusal precedence over MISSING-DEPENDENCY and OUTAGE.
whyThisIsSmallerThanItLooks.howToReadTheDeltas: Every count describing the purge MECHANISM is unchanged. The two that move are one added forbidden input, which only narrows what a function may read, and one added record type, which is configuration and touches no reviewed shape.

fieldTypes.retentionPolicyId: RETENTION-POLICY-ID-V1 string; names the consent-bearing policy this record is subordinate to

theDefaultIsUnbounded.statedBy: the recorded product intent of 2026-08-05: retention is durable by default, and UNBOUNDED unless configured
theDefaultIsUnbounded.whyTheDefaultIsNotWrittenIntoTheRecord: Same reasoning as the posture default: a default written into every project's record cannot be told apart from a choice, and changing it would mean migrating records rather than editing one function. The bounds resolution mirrors the posture resolution exactly.
theDefaultIsUnbounded.whyUnboundedRatherThanTheShippingProduct: The authority said unbounded unless configured. Adopting 200 / 60 days / 150 MB as silent defaults would mean a user who configured nothing nevertheless has evidence purged on a schedule they never chose. It would also quietly restore the position the authority overrode, by making durable-by-default mean durable-for-sixty-days.

effectiveBoundsResolution.signature: effective_bounds(boundsOrAbsent: ProjectRetentionBoundsV1 | ABSENT) -> (maxAgeSeconds, maxTotalBytes, keepCount, provenance: BoundsProvenance)
effectiveBoundsResolution.whyKeepTheDistinctionWhenBothPurgeNothin: The observable purge behaviour is identical today, which is exactly why the distinction must be structural rather than behavioural. If ABSENT were collapsed into all-zero, then the day anyone introduces a non-zero default upstream, every project that never configured retention silently acquires it. Keeping the states distinct means a bound can only ever arrive by someone writing a value into a record someone created. It is also the same consent-provenance shape Part A needs, applied to configuration.

residence.store: host-owned project storage under projects/<ProjectId>/, alongside the project retention policy and the availability ledger
residence.why: This is where the shipping product's shape is NOT adopted. The product keeps these knobs in a configuration file. In this corpus a resolved configuration layer is a place CI cannot see: the freeze records that CI and non-interactive mode never load or resolve layer 4. Bounds in a resolved layer would mean the same project retains different amounts of evidence depending on how it was invoked, invisibly. Host-owned project storage is neither a resolution layer nor inside the analysis snapshot root, so the PlanId exclusion is structural and the value is identical under every invocation profile.

boundsRecord.whyPostureAndConsentAreForbiddenHere: Two provenances must not be mixed in one record. posture and consentRecordRef are CONSENT-derived: they exist because a human was asked a question whose exact text digests into the consent record. maxAgeSeconds, maxTotalBytes and keepCount are CONFIGURATION-derived: nobody is asked. Letting a configuration record carry a posture would let configuration answer the consent question.

identity.preimage: UTF8(domainUtf8) || 0x00 || u16be(recipeVersion=1) || u16be(fieldCount=6) || frame(0x01, projectId) || frame(0x02, retentionPolicyId) || 0x03 || u32be(8) || u64be(maxAgeSeconds) || 0x04 || u32be(8) || u64be(maxTotalBytes) || 0x05 || u32be(8) || u64be(keepCount) || 0x06 || u32be(8) || u64be(boundsRevision)
identity.digest: SHA-256 over the complete preimage; textual form is rbnd1:sha256:<64 lowercase hex>
excluded: the current footprint of the project
any field of any other project's bounds record
identity.separateIdentityRule: Freeze law 6: separate identities keep separate descriptors and separate recipes. This is why the bounds are NOT added as a seventh field of ProjectRetentionPolicyV1. Adding a field there would change that record's field set while RETENTION-POLICY-ID-V1 declares recipeVersion 1 over fieldCount 3, so either the recipe stops describing the record, or the policy identity is re-minted every time an operator adjusts a storage knob.
identity.whyReMintingThePolicyIdentityWouldBeWron: retentionPolicyId is the identity of a CONSENT-bearing record: it is what consentRecordRef and policyRevision hang from. If changing maxTotalBytes re-minted it, an operator lowering a disk cap would produce a new policy identity, and either the consent record would have to be re-obtained for a storage tweak, or the same consent would be re-pointed at a new identity.

referenceDirection.statement: ProjectRetentionBoundsV1 carries retentionPolicyId. ProjectRetentionPolicyV1 carries no reference to the bounds.
referenceDirection.whyNotTheOtherDirection: A pointer from the policy to the bounds would put a mutable configuration digest inside the consent-bearing record, re-minting the policy identity on every knob change. Pointing the other way keeps the mutable thing downstream of the stable thing.
whatThisEnforces: Bounds cannot exist without a policy: a bounds record whose retentionPolicyId names no persisted policy for this projectId is refused at admission.

Bounds cannot outlive the consent they were configured under: when the policy is revised its retentionPolicyId changes, and a bounds record naming the superseded identity is refused until re-stated against the current policy.
Configuration can never answer the consent question, because configuration is the side that must NAME the answer, not the side that supplies it.

interactionWithTheDefaultedPosture.case: a project with no policy at all, whose posture therefore resolves DURABLE_RETAINED with provenance DEFAULTED
interactionWithTheDefaultedPosture.why: There is no persisted policy for a bounds record to name, so no bounds record can be admitted. A defaulted posture is not a persisted policy and does not become one.
interactionWithTheDefaultedPosture.consequence: The default configuration -- durable, unbounded, unasked -- is also the UNBOUNDABLE configuration until someone answers the retention question. A user cannot cap their disk usage without first being asked, or asking, about retention.
interactionWithTheDefaultedPosture.isThatAcceptable: IT IS A CONSEQUENCE, NOT A CHOICE MADE HERE
interactionWithTheDefaultedPosture.whyItIsFlagged: It is the least obvious interaction between the two recorded intents, and it points the wrong way: the configuration most in need of a bound is the one that cannot have one. An alternative -- letting bounds name a projectId rather than a policy identity -- would fix it and would also let configuration exist with no consent record behind it. This artifact does not choose between those; it names the tension.

referenceDirection.statedCost: Re-consenting forces bounds to be re-stated. That is deliberate: a bounds record silently surviving a change of posture would be a configuration outliving the consent that justified it.

protectedSet.derivation: A record is protected exactly when purging it would violate an invariant that already holds. This artifact therefore introduces NO protected list: the protected set is already fully determined by the independently verified Part B.

membersAndTheInvariantThatProtectsThem.member: every entry of UnitAvailabilityLedgerV1, which is to say every tombstone
every one of the 16 members of purgeMutationBoundary.doesNotMutate, including the sealed Run, the closure commitment, the evidence digest, PlanId and SnapshotId
membersAndTheInvariantThatProtectsThem.protectedBy: RT23-B-INV-04, which states that purge mutates exactly two things and no member of doesNotMutate
they are not raw objects in the project CAS; purge acts only on raw object bytes under projects/<ProjectId>/objects/

protectedSet.whyDerivingItMattered: An enumerated protected list would be a second place the truth is written, and the two would drift. Deriving it from doesNotMutate means the protected set changes only when the mutation boundary changes, and the mutation boundary is what a reviewer already checks.

evictableSet.definition: the raw objects under projects/<ProjectId>/objects/ whose current folded availability state is AVAILABLE, in the ledger of exactly this ProjectId
evictableSet.whyFoldedStateAndNotDiskContents: The ledger fold is the authority on what state a raw key is in. A record already PURGED has no bytes to reclaim and re-purging is idempotent, so including it would inflate every demand without freeing anything. A record in MISSING-DEPENDENCY is already absent from CAS. A record in OUTAGE is present but unreadable now.
evictableSet.whyOutageIsNeverEvictable: OUTAGE is reversible and PURGED is terminal. A sweep that evicted during an outage would turn a transient store problem into permanent evidence loss, and the ledger would honestly record it as an authorized retention action, which it was not. This is law 14 applied directly: a provider fault must not become something else.

sweep.theCentralStructuralProperty: A bound is a purge TRIGGER, not an admission GATE. Bounds select what to purge; they have no authority over whether a write is admitted. Everything else in this section follows from that one sentence, including what happens when a bound cannot be satisfied.
sweep.mutationBoundaryUnchanged: purgeMutationBoundary.mutatesExactly still has exactly two members. The sweep is a new CALLER of that boundary, not a new boundary.

neverRunsWhenBoundsAreDefaulted.statement: with provenance DEFAULTED the three values are 0, every demand is 0, and the sweep emits nothing

evictionOrder.order: ascending atSequence of the raw key's most recent AVAILABLE-entering ledger entry, tiebroken by recordCasRef lexicographic ascending
evictionOrder.adoptedFrom: the shipping product's oldest-first eviction, ordered (timestamp, id) ASC
evictionOrder.departedIn: the ordering key is the project ledger's atSequence, not a wall-clock timestamp
evictionOrder.whyLedgerSequenceRatherThanAClock: atSequence is already specified as strictly increasing by exactly one, with a break refused, so the ledger already carries a total order that is durable, host-owned, monotone and clock-free. A wall clock is none of those: it moves under NTP correction, is not monotone across a restart, and makes eviction order depend on a value no reviewer can reproduce. The tiebreak on recordCasRef makes the order total rather than a preorder, so two hosts folding the same ledger evict the same prefix in the same order.
evictionOrder.whySameOrderForEveryDimension: Derived from the composition requirement, not chosen for efficiency. With ONE order the set each bound wants removed is a PREFIX, and prefixes are totally ordered by inclusion, so the union of several demands is exactly the longest of them. With per-dimension orders the evicted set would be a union of incomparable sets, and disabling one bound could change WHICH records another bound removes rather than merely how many. Independence of bounds is a consequence of the single order.
evictionOrder.statedCostOfTheSingleOrder: Oldest-first is not size-optimal. Freeing N bytes may evict many small old records where one large recent record would have sufficed. Accepted deliberately: evicting largest-first would mean a user's most recent analysis disappears because it was big, which is harder to explain and destroys the prefix property. The shipping product also uses oldest-first for its size pruning, so this is agreement rather than departure.

demands.definition: each bound independently computes a DEMAND: the length of the prefix of the eviction order it requires to be removed

rows.whySatisfiable: len(evictable) is a fold of the ledger and needs no input that does not exist

rows.demand: the smallest k such that total_bytes(evictable[k:]) <= maxTotalBytes, or len(evictable) if no such k exists
rows.whySatisfiable: the byte length of a raw object is the length of the bytes at projects/<ProjectId>/objects/<recordKind>/sha256/<digestHex>, which the host measures directly; no schema field is required and none is added

rows.demand: the number of leading members of the eviction order whose admission time is older than now - maxAgeSeconds
rows.whyNotSatisfiable: no reviewed surface in this corpus records a per-raw-object admission time; see DEP-RT25-01

demands.evictedSet: the first evictionCount members of the eviction order
demands.whyMaxAndNotSum: Each demand is a prefix LENGTH, not a set. Removing the longest demanded prefix satisfies every shorter demand simultaneously, because a shorter prefix is contained in a longer one. Summing would evict records no bound asked for.

boundIndependence.property: each demand is a pure function of exactly two things: the eviction order, and that one bound's own configured value
boundIndependence.proof: Disabling a bound sets its demand to 0. max is monotone in each argument, so max(0, d_size, d_count) >= d_size and >= d_count hold unconditionally. Disabling any one dimension therefore cannot reduce what any other dimension demands. No expression contains one bound's value inside another bound's demand, so there is nothing to short-circuit.

theDefectThisRefusesToInherit.shape: the size bound is computed inside the count bound's branch, guarded by a test of the form: if the aggressive keep is <= 0 or the configured keep is <= 1, return early
theDefectThisRefusesToInherit.consequence: with keep set to 0 or 1, maxSizeMb silently deletes nothing; a user who disables count pruning loses size pruning and is not told
theDefectThisRefusesToInherit.whyAListOfPlacesWouldNotHaveFixedIt: The defect is not that one guard sits in the wrong place. It is that the size demand was expressed in terms of the count configuration at all. Enumerating branches to fix leaves the shape that produced them intact. Making each demand a pure function of its own configured value and the shared order makes the class unrepresentable: there is no term in which another bound's value could appear.
theDefectThisRefusesToInherit.structuralPropertyThatReplacesTheList: demand_X depends on X's configured value and the eviction order, and on nothing else

disableSemantics.adoptedFrom: the shipping product, where 0 disables a dimension
disableSemantics.agreesWithTheDefault: the defaulted bounds are 0 / 0 / 0, so the default is expressible in the same vocabulary a user would type
disableSemantics.whatTheProductDoes: a negative or non-finite configured value silently reverts to the built-in default, not to 0
disableSemantics.whyThatIsRefusedHere: Silently substituting a default for an invalid value means a user who typed -1 intending to disable a dimension gets the default bound instead, and their evidence is purged by a rule they explicitly tried to switch off. The failure is silent, the direction is toward MORE deletion, and nothing reports it.
disableSemantics.structuralRepair: There is no code path mapping an invalid value to a valid one, because admission rejects the record before any mapping exists. This is not a check an implementer must remember to write; it is the absence of the substitution.

howAnInvalidConfigurationIsReported.whyNoNewCodeIsRequested: CONFIG.INVALID is already a member of the live closed D9 error-code vocabulary, measured from the pinned bytes. An invalid retention bound is an invalid configuration and needs no new spelling.

anUnsatisfiableBoundIsRefusedNeverIgnore.rule: if maxAgeSeconds is non-zero while no per-raw-object admission time exists, the bounds record is REFUSED at admission with CONFIG.INVALID
anUnsatisfiableBoundIsRefusedNeverIgnore.why: Silently ignoring a bound the system cannot evaluate is the parasitic size bound wearing different clothes: the user configures a limit, the limit does nothing, and nothing says so. Refusing makes the missing input forcing, so the time dimension cannot ship until DEP-RT25-01 is resolved.
anUnsatisfiableBoundIsRefusedNeverIgnore.consequenceStatedPlainly: Until DEP-RT25-01 resolves, maxAgeSeconds can only be 0. The time dimension is specified and unusable. Count, which the shipping product reports as primary, and size are both usable today.

whenTheBoundCannotBeSatisfied.question: a bound is reached, and the protected set alone exceeds it. Refuse the write, or proceed degraded?
whenTheBoundCannotBeSatisfied.answer: PROCEED. The write is admitted. The sweep evicts everything evictable and stops, because it has run out of things to purge.

whyNotRefuseTheWrite.lawVerbatim: A durability failure cannot report authoritative success; a provider fault cannot become a finding; a policy failure cannot become a host error.
whyNotRefuseTheWrite.argument: A retention bound is a POLICY dimension: it sits in a host-owned, project-scoped record subordinate to a consent-bearing policy. Refusing an analysis write because a retention bound cannot be satisfied converts a policy failure into a host error, which is law 14's third clause named exactly.
After the refusal the bound is still exceeded, byte for byte. Refusal trades a real and recorded degradation for a total loss of function while leaving the storage condition unchanged.

whyNotRefuseTheWrite.reason: the condition is structurally unfixable, so it cannot be a gate
whyNotRefuseTheWrite.argument: The protected set is exactly the ledger plus the 16 members of doesNotMutate, and RT23-B-INV-04 states purge mutates none of them. So when the protected set alone exceeds the bound, no retention policy whatsoever can bring the project under it. A gate whose condition no configuration can satisfy is not a gate, it is an outage with a policy-shaped excuse.

whenTheBoundCannotBeSatisfied.whyNotWarnAndProceedEither: A warning is not an addressable state. It goes to a log, it is not derivable by a second reader, and nothing can be asserted about it. The product's oversize_unresolved is a string in a stream.

whatIsDoneInstead.predicate: over_bound(project) := footprint(project) > maxTotalBytes AND evictable(project) is empty
whatIsDoneInstead.why: Both operands are already readable: the footprint is measurable from the project store and the evictable set is a fold of the ledger. A recorded shortfall event would be a fourth thing that can go stale.
whatIsDoneInstead.consistencyWithSection46: This is the identical move section 4.6 verified for capability: do not record a derived fact, derive it at read time from state that cannot go stale. A second reader computes the same over_bound answer from the same bytes without consulting anything this artifact writes.

overBoundDoesNotLowerCapability.statement: being over bound is not an evidence-semantics condition and must not touch effectiveCapability
overBoundDoesNotLowerCapability.why: Over bound with nothing evictable means the project holds MORE evidence than it asked to keep. Every object is still AVAILABLE, so every unit_satisfied predicate still holds and the derivation still returns the sealed ceiling. Nothing is missing, nothing is refused, no caller is misled. It is a disk-space fact and belongs to operability.
overBoundDoesNotLowerCapability.operabilityPosition: G5 remains IMPLEMENTABLE and unclaimed, as RT23-B-RES-03 already states; this artifact makes no operability claim.

scope.derivation: A global bound is structurally unrepresentable in this corpus, not merely undesirable. Computing a global demand requires aggregating across project ledgers. UnitAvailabilityLedgerV1 is one ProjectId per ledger, matching freeze law 8, and effectiveCapabilityDerivation.forbiddenInputs already names ledgerSequenceOfAnyOtherProject. There is no global ledger to fold and reading another project's is already forbidden.
supportingFacts: ProjectRetentionPolicyV1.scope is ONE-PROJECT-ID and its owner is HOST
UnitAvailabilityLedgerV1.projectScope: one ProjectId per ledger; a purge in one project never reaches an identical digest in another
scope.statedConsequence: There is no global disk ceiling and this artifact does not supply one. N projects each configured with maxTotalBytes M can occupy N*M. Under durable-by-default and unbounded-by-default, N unconfigured projects occupy an unbounded total. That is declared here rather than discovered later.

causeVocabulary.whatChanges: the field's VALUE SET is closed for toState PURGED. No field is added, renamed or reordered.
causeVocabulary.admissionRule: cause is admitted as a JSON string at exact type before its content is compared, per freeze section 6 law 18. A boolean is not a string, a number is not a string and null is not a string, at any depth, including inside records the host only forwards.

meanings.RETENTION_AGE_BOUND: the record was older than maxAgeSeconds when the sweep ran
meanings.RETENTION_SIZE_BOUND: the record was in the prefix the size demand required in order to bring the project under maxTotalBytes
meanings.RETENTION_COUNT_BOUND: the record was in the prefix the count demand required in order to leave keepCount records
meanings.RETENTION_USER_REQUEST: a person asked for this record to be purged; no bound fired

attributionRuleWhenSeveralDemandsCover.rule: when more than one demand covers the same record, the cause recorded is the one belonging to the LARGEST demand, and ties break in the fixed order RETENTION_AGE_BOUND, RETENTION_SIZE_BOUND, RETENTION_COUNT_BOUND
attributionRuleWhenSeveralDemandsCover.why: The eviction count is the max of the demands, so the demand that actually decided the boundary is the largest one. Recording a smaller demand's name would tell a user to raise a knob that was not binding, which is worse than silence because it is actionable and wrong. The tiebreak is fixed so two hosts folding the same ledger record the same cause.
attributionRuleWhenSeveralDemandsCover.whyNotASetOfCauses: A ledger entry records one transition of one raw key. A set would make the field's type depend on how many demands happened to overlap, defeating exact-type admission and giving a reader no single answer to why this record is gone.

unclosedPartitions.reason: this artifact has no product intent behind an outage cause vocabulary and does not invent one
same; the transition already exists and its cause vocabulary is not this artifact's to close

causeVocabulary.whyOnlyThePurgedPartitionIsClosed: The recorded product intent concerns retention bounds and why a purged record is gone. It says nothing about outages or missing dependencies. Closing those partitions here would be inventing vocabulary with no authority behind it, and a closed enum is far harder to reopen than an open one is to close. The property the intent asks for -- a PURGED state always says why -- is fully delivered by closing exactly one partition.

tombstoneAlwaysExplainsAbsence.statement: for every raw key whose folded state is PURGED there is a ledger entry, it is permanent, and it names one of exactly four reasons

aPurgeCausedByAPostureChangeHasNoMember.case: the posture is revised from DURABLE_RETAINED to EPHEMERAL_ONLY and existing durable evidence is purged as a result
aPurgeCausedByAPostureChangeHasNoMember.nowMoreLikelyThanBefore: Under durable-by-default this case stops being hypothetical. Every project starts DURABLE_RETAINED by default, so the first time a user is asked and answers EPHEMERAL_ONLY, there may already be durable evidence on disk that was written under the default. What happens to it is exactly this unresolved case, and the posture decision makes it the common path rather than an edge case.
aPurgeCausedByAPostureChangeHasNoMember.couldItBeFoldedIntoUserRequest: arguably, since a person changed the policy
aPurgeCausedByAPostureChangeHasNoMember.whyItIsNotFoldedHere: Whether opting out of durable retention deletes evidence already retained is a product question, not an architecture one, and it is adjacent to the CD-RT-5 choice that remains BLOCKED_ON_PHASE_1A. Folding it into RETENTION_USER_REQUEST would answer that question by naming, which is the mechanism section 4.5 exists to prevent.

d9ReasonCodePosition.authority: D9 owns the closed termination vocabulary; this artifact may not amend a vocabulary it does not own, and does not.

measuredLiveFromPinnedD9Bytes.measuredStatement: 0 of 9 deficiency members, 0 of 9 reason codes and 0 of 19 error codes name retention-driven read-time unavailability
measuredLiveFromPinnedD9Bytes.howMeasured: reason codes and error codes counted from codeVocabulary.reasonCodes and codeVocabulary.errorCodes; deficiency members from codeMaps.deficiencyToReasonCode keys; the token predicate applied to each name uppercased
measuredLiveFromPinnedD9Bytes.whyTheCountsAreTakenFromCodeVocabularyAn: the union of the two cause-to-error-code maps has 18 distinct values, because SYSTEM.OUTCOME.ILLEGAL_STATE appears in codeVocabulary.errorCodes and in neither map. The predecessor's figure of 19 is the codeVocabulary count and is the correct one; this artifact measured both and records the difference so a later reader does not have to rediscover it.

whyOneAndNotFour.question: the cause partition has four members. Does the D9 request become four reason codes?
whyOneAndNotFour.answer: No. One reason code, four causes.
whyOneAndNotFour.d9OwnRuleVerbatim: two codes with the same remedy are a smell and two remedies behind one code are a defect
whyOneAndNotFour.derivation: The remedy behind all four causes is identical: the evidence was removed by an authorized project retention action, cannot be restored by this tool, and the analysis must be re-run to produce new evidence. Four codes carrying one remedy is precisely the smell D9's own rule names. What differs between the four is not the remedy but the EXPLANATION, and an explanation of a cause is what a cause field is for. The four-way split therefore belongs on AvailabilityTransitionV1.cause and the single remedy on the reason code.
whyOneAndNotFour.consequence: The predecessor's single proposed reason code is confirmed unchanged, now with a derivation behind it rather than an absence of alternatives.

requestedSuccessorNotAdded.authority: this artifact may not amend a closed vocabulary it does not own
requestedSuccessorNotAdded.proposedRemedy: the evidence was removed by an authorized project retention action and cannot be restored by this tool; re-run the analysis to produce new evidence
requestedSuccessorNotAdded.whatThisArtifactAddsToTheRequest: the remedy text may now render the specific cause, because the cause is a closed four-member partition rather than an unstated string. That refines the request's payload; it does not change the number of codes.

doesThisCloseRT23BRES01.theRecordedIntentSaysItDoes: The prepared amendment draft states, under reasonCodeRequired, that the reason-code requirement 'closes residual RT23-B-RES-01'. Measured against the live pinned D9 bytes that is not what happens, and this artifact reports the measurement rather than the expectation.
doesThisCloseRT23BRES01.measuredJustification: RT23-B-RES-01's closing condition is d9VocabularyMembersNamingRetentionLoss becoming non-zero. Measured live from the pinned D9 bytes at authoring time it is 0, exactly as the predecessor measured it. This artifact adds nothing to D9, so it cannot and does not move that number.
doesThisCloseRT23BRES01.residualClosesWhen: a D9 successor adds one deficiency member and one reason code. Still not addable here.
doesThisCloseRT23BRES01.whatThisArtifactDoesCloseInstead: a different and previously unnamed gap: the PURGED STATE itself carried no reason. Before this artifact a purged record was terminal, permanent and silent about why. After it, every PURGED ledger entry names one of four causes. That is the architecture-side half of explainability and is wholly within this artifact's authority. The D9-side half remains open.
doesThisCloseRT23BRES01.whyItWouldBeWrongToClaimOtherwise: Claiming closure would require either adding a D9 member without authority, or restating the residual so its measured boundary no longer describes what it was measuring. The predecessor declined to pick a dishonest in-vocabulary code and this artifact declines to pick a dishonest closure.

section46DischargePreservation.obligationVerbatim: State how purge changes current evidence availability without rewriting the sealed Run
whatWasIndependentlyVerified: both sealed unitIds recompute byte-exactly, two-sided control holds
all four of v22's fixtures including AF-03-VERIFY-PURGED derive and agree
P1, P2 and P5 reproduced at 276/276, 276/276 and 46/46
P4 verified in the strong form: result equals min(sealed, best) at all 276
purge never raises capability across 40,000 randomised multi-position trials, zero counterexamples
append-only survived hostile ledgers: terminal reversal, sequence break, restart and non-1 start all refused
section46DischargePreservation.doesTheDischargeSurvive: YES, BY CONSTRUCTION, AND UNVERIFIED ON THESE BYTES

triggers.claim: triggers cannot disturb any verified property
triggers.argument: effective_capability takes exactly three inputs: sealedCapability, units and availabilityRecords. A trigger changes only WHICH AvailabilityTransitionV1 entries come to exist and WHEN. It adds no input, changes no input's type, and touches no term of the algorithm. P1, P2, P3 and P4 are statements about the function and the function is unchanged.

neverRaisesCapability.claim: a sweep can only lower or preserve effectiveCapability, never raise it
neverRaisesCapability.argument: A sweep emits entries with toState PURGED and no other toState. unit_satisfied requires EVERY state in the unit's position map to be AVAILABLE. Moving any position from AVAILABLE to PURGED can only falsify unit_satisfied for the units containing it and can falsify no fewer. satisfied() is downward closed in rank by P3, so the set of satisfied capabilities can only shrink and its maximum can only fall or stay. Monotone by construction; no trials needed.

causeVocabulary.claim: closing the cause partition cannot change any derived capability
causeVocabulary.argument: The fold rule states the current state of a raw key is the toState of its last entry. cause is not toState and the algorithm reads no other field of a ledger entry. cause is already unreachable from the derivation, and adding members to a field the function never reads changes nothing it can compute.
causeVocabulary.whyItIsTheRiskiest: P5-CAUSE-BLIND is the one verified property whose subject matter this artifact touches. P5 states cause-blindness ACROSS STATES. Introducing sub-causes of PURGED raises the adjacent question of blindness WITHIN a state, which P5 does not state.

p5Extended.statement: any two ledger entries agreeing on toState and differing only in cause derive the same effectiveCapability
p5Extended.relationToP5: STRICTLY STRONGER: P5 is blindness across states, this is blindness across causes within a state
p5Extended.whyAlreadyTrue: the algorithm reads only toState from a ledger entry, so cause has no path into the result
p5Extended.howItIsMadeStructuralRatherThanIncidenta: cause is added to effectiveCapabilityDerivation.forbiddenInputs, taking that list from 11 members to 12. It was already unread; naming it forbidden makes the property checkable by a reviewer who greps the derivation rather than inferrable from the absence of a mention.
p5Extended.monotonicityOfTheChange: Adding a member to forbiddenInputs can only reduce the set of inputs the function may read. It can never admit an input previously refused. So the change cannot weaken P1, P2, P3, P4 or P5, and this direction holds without re-running anything.

thePostureDecisionDoesNotTouchPartB.statement: the durable-by-default decision changes Part A and changes nothing in Part B
thePostureDecisionDoesNotTouchPartB.why: Part B is about what happens to evidence that exists. The posture decides whether evidence comes to exist. No availability state, no ledger rule, no term of effective_capability and no member of the mutation boundary mentions the posture, and none needs to.

whatIsNotClaimed: That the 40,000-trial result travels to these bytes. It was run by an independent reviewer over the predecessor's bytes and is bound to those digests. This artifact re-ran nothing.
That V10 item 3 discharges on these bytes. The discharge is the predecessor's, on the predecessor's digests.

Refusing converts a policy failure into a host error against law 14, reclaims no bytes, and gates on a condition that RT23-B-INV-04 makes structurally unsatisfiable. answeredQuestions.justification: oldest-first is adopted from the shipping product; the ordering KEY departs from it, using the ledger sequence rather than a wall clock so the order is monotone, durable and reproducible. The sharing is derived: with one order each demand is a prefix length, prefixes are totally ordered by inclusion, and the union of demands is exactly the longest — which is what makes the bounds independent. Per-dimension orders would let disabling one bound change which records another removes.
